claim: Metastasis is responsible for approximately 90% of cancer-associated mortality.
source: Metastasis is responsible for approximately 90% of cancer-associated mortality but few models exist that allow for rapid and effective screening of anti-metastasis drugs.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field of cancer research, commonly cited in the literature.

claim: At least 50 common genes are involved in both metastasis and gastrulation progression.
source: At least 50 common genes were shown to be involved in both metastasis and gastrulation progression: Knockdown of these genes in Xenopus or zebrafish induced gastrulation defects; conversely, overexpression of these genes conferred metastatic potential on cancer cells and knockdown of these genes suppressed metastasis (Yang and Weinberg, 2008; Dongre and Weinberg, 2019; Thiery et al., 2009; Nieto et al., 2016; Table 1).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature and reference to Table 1 which lists the 50 genes.

claim: The screen tested 1280 FDA-approved drugs.
source: The screen tested 1280 FDA-approved drugs and identified pizotifen, an antagonist for serotonin receptor 2C (HTR2C) as an epiboly-interrupting drug.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design and number of drugs screened.

claim: Pizotifen is an antagonist for serotonin receptor 2C (HTR2C).
source: The screen tested 1280 FDA-approved drugs and identified pizotifen, an antagonist for serotonin receptor 2C (HTR2C) as an epiboly-interrupting drug.
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge about the drug pizotifen.

claim: Pizotifen was identified as an epiboly-interrupting drug.
source: The screen tested 1280 FDA-approved drugs and identified pizotifen, an antagonist for serotonin receptor 2C (HTR2C) as an epiboly-interrupting drug.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the screening experiment described in the manuscript.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of HTR2C suppressed metastatic progression in a mouse model.
source: Pharmacological and genetic inhibition of HTR2C suppressed metastatic progression in a mouse model.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the mouse experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Genetic inhibition of HTR2C suppressed metastatic progression in a mouse model.
source: Pharmacological and genetic inhibition of HTR2C suppressed metastatic progression in a mouse model.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the mouse experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Blocking HTR2C with pizotifen restored epithelial properties to metastatic cells through inhibition of Wnt signaling.
source: Blocking HTR2C with pizotifen restored epithelial properties to metastatic cells through inhibition of Wnt signaling.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: HTR2C induced epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through activation of Wnt signaling.
source: In contrast, HTR2C induced epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through activation of Wnt signaling and promoted metastatic dissemination of human cancer cells in a zebrafish xenotransplantation model.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: HTR2C promoted metastatic dissemination of human cancer cells in a zebrafish xenotransplantation model.
source: In contrast, HTR2C induced epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through activation of Wnt signaling and promoted metastatic dissemination of human cancer cells in a zebrafish xenotransplantation model.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the zebrafish xenotransplantation experiments.

claim: Metastasis occurs through multiple steps: invasion, intravasation, extravasation, colonization, and metastatic tumor formation.
source: Metastasis, a leading contributor to the morbidity of cancer patients, occurs through multiple steps: invasion, intravasation, extravasation, colonization, and metastatic tumor formation (Nguyen et al., 2009; Welch and Hurst, 2019; Chaffer and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The physical translocation of cancer cells is an initial step of metastasis.
source: The physical translocation of cancer cells is an initial step of metastasis and molecular mechanisms of it involve cell motility, the breakdown of local basement membrane, loss of cell polarity, acquisition of stem cell-like properties, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Tsai and Yang, 2013; Lu and Kang, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Molecular mechanisms of metastatic translocation involve cell motility, the breakdown of local basement membrane, loss of cell polarity, acquisition of stem cell-like properties, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
source: The physical translocation of cancer cells is an initial step of metastasis and molecular mechanisms of it involve cell motility, the breakdown of local basement membrane, loss of cell polarity, acquisition of stem cell-like properties, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Tsai and Yang, 2013; Lu and Kang, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Cell-biological phenomena observed in metastasis are also observed during vertebrate gastrulation.
source: These cell-biological phenomena are also observed during vertebrate gastrulation in that evolutionarily conserved morphogenetic movements of epiboly, internalization, convergence, and extension progress (Solnica-Krezel, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental biology, supported by citation.

claim: In zebrafish, epiboly is initiated at approximately 4 hr post fertilization (hpf).
source: In zebrafish, the first morphogenetic movement, epiboly, is initiated at approximately 4 hr post fertilization (hpf) to move cells from the animal pole to eventually engulf the entire yolk cell by 10 hpf (Latimer and Jessen, 2010; Solnica-Krezel, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish development, supported by citations.

claim: Epiboly in zebrafish moves cells from the animal pole to eventually engulf the entire yolk cell by 10 hpf.
source: In zebrafish, the first morphogenetic movement, epiboly, is initiated at approximately 4 hr post fertilization (hpf) to move cells from the animal pole to eventually engulf the entire yolk cell by 10 hpf (Latimer and Jessen, 2010; Solnica-Krezel, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish development, supported by citations.

claim: Gene set enrichment analysis demonstrated that 50%-epiboly, shield, and 75%-epiboly stage of zebrafish embryos expressed genes which promote EMT-mediated metastasis.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) demonstrated that 50%-epiboly, shield, and 75%-epiboly stage of zebrafish embryos expressed the genes which promote EMT-mediated metastasis: EMT induction, TGF-β signaling, wnt/β-catenin signaling, Notch signaling (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the GSEA analysis performed in the study, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Elevated expression of PRMT1 was observed in highly metastatic human breast cancer cell lines.
source: Elevated expression of PRMT1 and CYP11A1 was observed in highly metastatic human breast cancer cell lines and knockdown of these genes through RNA interference suppressed the motility and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells without affecting their viability (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: This is a finding from the western blot analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Elevated expression of CYP11A1 was observed in highly metastatic human breast cancer cell lines.
source: Elevated expression of PRMT1 and CYP11A1 was observed in highly metastatic human breast cancer cell lines and knockdown of these genes through RNA interference suppressed the motility and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells without affecting their viability (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: This is a finding from the western blot analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Knockdown of PRMT1 through RNA interference suppressed the motility and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells without affecting their viability.
source: Elevated expression of PRMT1 and CYP11A1 was observed in highly metastatic human breast cancer cell lines and knockdown of these genes through RNA interference suppressed the motility and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells without affecting their viability (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Knockdown of CYP11A1 through RNA interference suppressed the motility and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells without affecting their viability.
source: Elevated expression of PRMT1 and CYP11A1 was observed in highly metastatic human breast cancer cell lines and knockdown of these genes through RNA interference suppressed the motility and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells without affecting their viability (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Niclosamide is reported to suppress metastatic progression.
source: Niclosamide and vinpocetine are reported to suppress metastatic progression (Weinbach and Garbus, 1969; Sack et al., 2011; Huang et al., 2012; Szilágyi et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature, supported by citations.

claim: Vinpocetine is reported to suppress metastatic progression.
source: Niclosamide and vinpocetine are reported to suppress metastatic progression (Weinbach and Garbus, 1969; Sack et al., 2011; Huang et al., 2012; Szilágyi et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature, supported by citations.

claim: Niclosamide-treated zebrafish embryos showed complete arrest at very early stages of epiboly progression.
source: Either niclosamide- or vinpocetine-treated zebrafish embryos showed complete arrest at very early stages or severe delay in epiboly progression, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the zebrafish experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Vinpocetine-treated zebrafish embryos showed severe delay in epiboly progression.
source: Either niclosamide- or vinpocetine-treated zebrafish embryos showed complete arrest at very early stages or severe delay in epiboly progression, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the zebrafish experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: 0.9% (12/1280) of the drugs induced severe or complete arrest of embryonic cell movement when embryos were treated with 10 μM.
source: The screening showed that 0.9% (12/1280) of the drugs, including antimycin A and tolcapone, induced severe or complete arrest of embryonic cell movement when embryos were treated with 10 μM.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screening experiment.

claim: 5.2% (66/1280) of the drugs induced either delayed epiboly or interrupted epiboly of the embryos when treated with 10 μM.
source: 5.2% (66/1280) of the drugs, such as dicumarol, racecadotril, pizotifen, and S(-)eticlopride hydrochloride, induced either delayed epiboly or interrupted epiboly of the embryos.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screening experiment.

claim: 93.3% (1194/1280) of drugs have no effect on epiboly progression of the embryos when treated with 10 μM.
source: 93.3% (1194/1280) of drugs have no effect on epiboly progression of the embryos.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screening experiment.

claim: 0.6% (8/1280) of drugs induced toxic lethality when treated with 10 μM.
source: 0.6% (8/1280) of drugs induced toxic lethality.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screening experiment.

claim: 1.7% (22/1280) of the drugs induced severe or complete arrest of epiboly when embryos were treated with 50 μM.
source: Epiboly progression was affected more severely when embryos were treated with 50 μM; 1.7% (22/1280) of the drugs induced severe or complete arrest of it.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screening experiment.

claim: 8.6% (110/1280) of the drugs induced either delayed epiboly or interrupt epiboly of the embryos when treated with 50 μM.
source: 8.6% (110/1280) of the drugs induced either delayed epiboly or interrupt epiboly of the embryos.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screening experiment.

claim: 4.3% (55/1280) of drugs induced a toxic lethality when treated with 50 μM.
source: 4.3% (55/1280) of drugs induced a toxic lethality (Figure 1A and B, Table 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screening experiment, shown in Figure 1A and B, Table 2.

claim: Adrenosterone targets HSD11β1.
source: adrenosterone or zardaverine, which target HSD11β1 or PDE3 and -4, respectively, are reported to inhibit EMT (Nakayama et al., 2020; Kolosionek et al., 2009)
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: Zardaverine targets PDE3 and PDE4.
source: adrenosterone or zardaverine, which target HSD11β1 or PDE3 and -4, respectively, are reported to inhibit EMT (Nakayama et al., 2020; Kolosionek et al., 2009)
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge, supported by citations.

source: racecadotril, which targets enkephalinase, is reported to confer metastatic potential on colon cancer cell (Sasaki et al., 2014)
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge, supported by citation.

claim: Racecadotril is reported to confer metastatic potential on colon cancer cells.
source: racecadotril, which targets enkephalinase, is reported to confer metastatic potential on colon cancer cell (Sasaki et al., 2014)
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature, supported by citation.

claim: Disulfiram targets ALDH (aldehyde dehydrogenase).
source: disulfiram, which targets ALDH (aldehyde dehydrogenase), is reported to confer stem-like properties on metastatic cancer cells (Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge, supported by citation.

claim: Disulfiram is reported to confer stem-like properties on metastatic cancer cells.
source: disulfiram, which targets ALDH (aldehyde dehydrogenase), is reported to confer stem-like properties on metastatic cancer cells (Liu et al., 2013).

claim: Out of 78 epiboly-interrupting drugs, 16 strongly affected cell viability at concentrations less than 1 μM.
source: Out of the 78 drugs, 16 of them strongly affected cell viability at concentrations less than 1 μM and were not used in the cell motility experiments.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the MTT assay experiments.

claim: Out of 62 drugs tested in Boyden chamber motility experiments, 20 inhibited cell motility and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells without affecting cell viability.
source: The remaining 62 drugs were assayed in Boyden chamber motility experiments. Out of the 62 drugs, 20 of the drugs inhibited cell motility and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells without affecting cell viability.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the Boyden chamber experiments.

claim: HTR2C expression is correlated with tumor stage of breast cancer patients.
source: Clinical data also shows that that HTR2C expression is correlated with tumor stage of breast cancer patients and is higher in metastatic and Her2/neu-overexpressing tumors (Pai et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge from clinical data, supported by citation.

claim: HTR2C expression is higher in metastatic and Her2/neu-overexpressing tumors.
source: Clinical data also shows that that HTR2C expression is correlated with tumor stage of breast cancer patients and is higher in metastatic and Her2/neu-overexpressing tumors (Pai et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge from clinical data, supported by citation.

claim: Pizotifen suppressed cell motility and invasion of several highly metastatic human cancer cell lines in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Pizotifen suppressed cell motility and invasion of several highly metastatic human cancer cell lines in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the Boyden chamber experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: DRD2 was highly expressed in only metastatic cell lines.
source: Similarly, dopamine receptor D2 (DRD2), which is a primary target of S(-)eticlopride hydrochloride, was highly expressed in only metastatic cell lines, and the drug suppressed cell motility and invasion of these cells in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: This is a finding from the western blot analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: S(-)eticlopride hydrochloride suppressed cell motility and invasion of metastatic cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Similarly, dopamine receptor D2 (DRD2), which is a primary target of S(-)eticlopride hydrochloride, was highly expressed in only metastatic cell lines, and the drug suppressed cell motility and invasion of these cells in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: This is a finding from the Boyden chamber experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: In the pizotifen-treated group, the frequencies of fish showing head dissemination significantly decreased to 55.3% ± 7.5% compared with 95.8% ± 5.8% in the vehicle-treated group.
source: Three independent experiments revealed that the frequencies of fish in the drug-treated group showing head, trunk, or end-tail dissemination significantly decreased to 55.3% ± 7.5%, 28.5 ± 5.0%, or 43.5% ± 19.1% when compared with those in the vehicle-treated group; 95.8% ± 5.8%, 47.1 ± 7.7%, or 82.6% ± 12.7%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the zebrafish xenotransplantation experiments.

claim: In the pizotifen-treated group, the frequencies of fish showing trunk dissemination significantly decreased to 28.5 ± 5.0% compared with 47.1 ± 7.7% in the vehicle-treated group.
source: Three independent experiments revealed that the frequencies of fish in the drug-treated group showing head, trunk, or end-tail dissemination significantly decreased to 55.3% ± 7.5%, 28.5 ± 5.0%, or 43.5% ± 19.1% when compared with those in the vehicle-treated group; 95.8% ± 5.8%, 47.1 ± 7.7%, or 82.6% ± 12.7%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the zebrafish xenotransplantation experiments.

claim: In the pizotifen-treated group, the frequencies of fish showing end-tail dissemination significantly decreased to 43.5% ± 19.1% compared with 82.6% ± 12.7% in the vehicle-treated group.
source: Three independent experiments revealed that the frequencies of fish in the drug-treated group showing head, trunk, or end-tail dissemination significantly decreased to 55.3% ± 7.5%, 28.5 ± 5.0%, or 43.5% ± 19.1% when compared with those in the vehicle-treated group; 95.8% ± 5.8%, 47.1 ± 7.7%, or 82.6% ± 12.7%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the zebrafish xenotransplantation experiments.

claim: The frequency of fish not showing any dissemination significantly increased to 45.4% ± 0.5% in the pizotifen-treated group compared with 2.0% ± 2.9% in the vehicle-treated group.
source: Conversely, the frequency of the fish in the drug-treated group not showing any dissemination significantly increased to 45.4% ± 0.5% when compared with those in the vehicle-treated group; 2.0% ± 2.9% (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Table 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the zebrafish xenotransplantation experiments, shown in Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Table 4.

claim: In fish inoculated with shHTR2C 231R cells, the frequencies of fish showing head dissemination significantly decreased to 6.7% ± 4.9% compared with 80.0% ± 27.1% in fish inoculated with shLacZ 231R cells.
source: In the fish that were inoculated with shHTR2C 231R cells, the frequencies of the fish showing head, trunk, and end-tail dissemination significantly decreased to 6.7% ± 4.9%, 6.7% ± 0.7%, or 20.0% ± 16.5%; conversely, the frequency of the fish not showing any dissemination significantly increased to 80.0% ± 4.4% when compared with those that were inoculated with shLacZ 231R cells; 80.0% ± 27.1%, 20.0% ± 4.5%, 90.0% ± 7.7%, or 0% (Figure 2E and Table 6).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the zebrafish xenotransplantation experiments with genetic knockdown, shown in Figure 2E and Table 6.

claim: In fish inoculated with shHTR2C 231R cells, the frequencies of fish showing trunk dissemination significantly decreased to 6.7% ± 0.7% compared with 20.0% ± 4.5% in fish inoculated with shLacZ 231R cells.
source: In the fish that were inoculated with shHTR2C 231R cells, the frequencies of the fish showing head, trunk, and end-tail dissemination significantly decreased to 6.7% ± 4.9%, 6.7% ± 0.7%, or 20.0% ± 16.5%; conversely, the frequency of the fish not showing any dissemination significantly increased to 80.0% ± 4.4% when compared with those that were inoculated with shLacZ 231R cells; 80.0% ± 27.1%, 20.0% ± 4.5%, 90.0% ± 7.7%, or 0% (Figure 2E and Table 6).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the zebrafish xenotransplantation experiments with genetic knockdown, shown in Figure 2E and Table 6.

claim: In fish inoculated with shHTR2C 231R cells, the frequencies of fish showing end-tail dissemination significantly decreased to 20.0% ± 16.5% compared with 90.0% ± 7.7% in fish inoculated with shLacZ 231R cells.
source: In the fish that were inoculated with shHTR2C 231R cells, the frequencies of the fish showing head, trunk, and end-tail dissemination significantly decreased to 6.7% ± 4.9%, 6.7% ± 0.7%, or 20.0% ± 16.5%; conversely, the frequency of the fish not showing any dissemination significantly increased to 80.0% ± 4.4% when compared with those that were inoculated with shLacZ 231R cells; 80.0% ± 27.1%, 20.0% ± 4.5%, 90.0% ± 7.7%, or 0% (Figure 2E and Table 6).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the zebrafish xenotransplantation experiments with genetic knockdown, shown in Figure 2E and Table 6.

claim: In fish inoculated with shHTR2C 231R cells, the frequency of fish not showing any dissemination significantly increased to 80.0% ± 4.4% compared with 0% in fish inoculated with shLacZ 231R cells.
source: In the fish that were inoculated with shHTR2C 231R cells, the frequencies of the fish showing head, trunk, and end-tail dissemination significantly decreased to 6.7% ± 4.9%, 6.7% ± 0.7%, or 20.0% ± 16.5%; conversely, the frequency of the fish not showing any dissemination significantly increased to 80.0% ± 4.4% when compared with those that were inoculated with shLacZ 231R cells; 80.0% ± 27.1%, 20.0% ± 4.5%, 90.0% ± 7.7%, or 0% (Figure 2E and Table 6).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the zebrafish xenotransplantation experiments with genetic knockdown, shown in Figure 2E and Table 6.

claim: The sizes of the primary tumors in pizotifen-treated mice were equal to those in the vehicle-treated mice on day 10 post inoculation.
source: Bioluminescence imaging and tumor measurement revealed that the sizes of the primary tumors in pizotifen-treated mice were equal to those in the vehicle-treated mice on day 10 post inoculation.
evidence: This is a finding from the mouse model experiments.

claim: The percentage of Ki67-positive cells in the resected primary tumors of pizotifen-treated mice were the same as those of vehicle-treated mice.
source: Immunofluorescence (IF) staining also demonstrated that the percentage of Ki67-positive cells in the resected primary tumors of pizotifen-treated mice were the same as those of vehicle-treated mice (Figure 3A–C)
evidence: This is a finding from the immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 3A–C.

claim: Both pizotifen-treated and vehicle-treated groups showed less than 1% cleaved caspase 3 positive cells.
source: additionally, both groups showed less than 1% cleaved caspase 3 positive cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: No anti-tumor effect of pizotifen was observed on the primary tumor.
source: Therefore, no anti-tumor effect of pizotifen was observed on the primary tumor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tumor size and proliferation marker data.

claim: Bioluminescence imaging detected light emitted in the lungs, livers, and lymph nodes of vehicle-treated mice but not those of pizotifen-treated mice after 70 days from inoculation.
source: After 70 days from inoculation, bioluminescence imaging detected light emitted in the lungs, livers, and lymph nodes of vehicle-treated mice but not those of pizotifen-treated mice (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the bioluminescence imaging shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Vehicle-treated mice formed 5–50 metastatic nodules per lung in all 10 mice analyzed.
source: Vehicle-treated mice formed 5–50 metastatic nodules per lung in all 10 mice analyzed; conversely, pizotifen-treated mice (n = 10) formed 0–5 nodules per lung in all 10 mice analyzed (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the histological analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Pizotifen-treated mice formed 0–5 nodules per lung in all 10 mice analyzed.
source: Vehicle-treated mice formed 5–50 metastatic nodules per lung in all 10 mice analyzed; conversely, pizotifen-treated mice (n = 10) formed 0–5 nodules per lung in all 10 mice analyzed (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the histological analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Metastatic lesions in the lungs were detected in all vehicle-treated mice.
source: Histological analyses confirmed that metastatic lesions in the lungs were detected in all vehicle-treated mice; conversely, they were detected in only 2 of 10 pizotifen-treated mice and the rest of the mice showed metastatic colony formations around the bronchiole of the lung.
evidence: This is a finding from the histological analysis.

claim: Metastatic lesions in the lungs were detected in only 2 of 10 pizotifen-treated mice.
source: Histological analyses confirmed that metastatic lesions in the lungs were detected in all vehicle-treated mice; conversely, they were detected in only 2 of 10 pizotifen-treated mice and the rest of the mice showed metastatic colony formations around the bronchiole of the lung.
evidence: This is a finding from the histological analysis.

claim: 4 of 10 vehicle-treated mice exhibited metastasis in the liver.
source: In addition, 4 of 10 vehicle-treated mice exhibited metastasis in the liver and the rest showed metastatic colony formation around the portal tract of the liver.
evidence: This is a finding from the histological analysis.

claim: None of 10 pizotifen-treated mice showed liver metastases.
source: In contrast, none of 10 pizotifen-treated mice showed liver metastases and only half of the 10 mice showed metastatic colony formation around the portal tract (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the histological analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Only half of the 10 pizotifen-treated mice showed metastatic colony formation around the portal tract.
source: In contrast, none of 10 pizotifen-treated mice showed liver metastases and only half of the 10 mice showed metastatic colony formation around the portal tract (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the histological analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Pizotifen can suppress metastasis progression without affecting primary tumor growth.
source: These results indicate that pizotifen can suppress metastasis progression without affecting primary tumor growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mouse model experiments.

claim: All of the mice (n = 5) that were inoculated with 4T1 cells expressing shRNA targeting LacZ showed metastases in the lungs.
source: Histological analyses revealed that all of the mice (n = 5) that were inoculated with 4T1 cells expressing shRNA targeting LacZ showed metastases in the lungs.
evidence: This is a finding from the histological analysis of the genetic knockdown experiments.

claim: The mean number of metastatic lesions in a lung was 26.4 ± 7.8 for mice inoculated with 4T1 cells expressing shRNA targeting LacZ.
source: The mean number of metastatic lesions in a lung was 26.4 ± 7.8.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the histological analysis of the genetic knockdown experiments.

claim: Only one of the mice (n = 5) inoculated with 4T1 cells expressing shRNA targeting HTR2C showed metastases in the lungs.
source: In contrast, only one of the mice (n = 5) were inoculated with 4T1 cells expressing shRNA targeting HTR2C showed metastases in the lungs and the rest of the mice showed metastatic colony formation around the bronchiole of the lung.
evidence: This is a finding from the histological analysis of the genetic knockdown experiments.

claim: The mean number of metastatic lesions in the lung significantly decreased to 10% of those of mice that were inoculated with 4T1 cells expressing shRNA targeting LacZ when HTR2C was knocked down.
source: The mean number of metastatic lesions in the lung significantly decreased to 10% of those of mice that were inoculated with 4T1 cells expressing shRNA targeting LacZ (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the histological analysis of the genetic knockdown experiments, shown in Figure 3F–H.

claim: HTR2C-expressing MCF7 cells led to loss of cell-cell contact and cell scattering.
source: Vector control expressing MCF7 cells maintained highly organized cell-cell adhesion and cell polarity; however, HTR2C-expressing MCF7 cells led to loss of cell-cell contact and cell scattering.
evidence: This is a morphological observation from the cell culture experiments.

claim: The cobblestone-like appearance of MCF7 cells was replaced by a spindle-like, fibroblastic morphology when HTR2C was expressed.
source: The cobblestone-like appearance of these cells was replaced by a spindle-like, fibroblastic morphology.
evidence: This is a morphological observation from the cell culture experiments.

claim: HTR2C-expressing MCF7 cells showed loss of E-cadherin and EpCAM.
source: Western blotting and IF analyses revealed that HTR2C-expressing MCF7 cells showed loss of E-cadherin and EpCAM, and elevated expressions of N-cadherin, vimentin, and an EMT-inducible transcriptional factor ZEB1.
evidence: This is a finding from the western blotting and IF analyses.

claim: HTR2C-expressing MCF7 cells showed elevated expressions of N-cadherin, vimentin, and ZEB1.
source: Western blotting and IF analyses revealed that HTR2C-expressing MCF7 cells showed loss of E-cadherin and EpCAM, and elevated expressions of N-cadherin, vimentin, and an EMT-inducible transcriptional factor ZEB1.
evidence: This is a finding from the western blotting and IF analyses.

claim: HTR2C-expressing HaCaT cells showed loss of cell-cell contact and cell scattering with loss of epithelial markers and gain of mesenchymal markers.
source: Similar effects were validated through another experiment using an immortal keratinocyte cell line, HaCaT cells, in that HTR2C-expressing HaCaT cells also showed loss of cell-cell contact and cell scattering with loss of epithelial markers and gain of mesenchymal markers (Figure 4A–C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments with HaCaT cells shown in Figure 4A–C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: HTR2C-expressing MCF7 cells had undergone an EMT.
source: Therefore, both the morphological and molecular changes in the HTR2C-expressing MCF7 and HaCaT cells demonstrated that these cells had undergone an EMT.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the morphological and molecular data.

claim: HTR2C expressing MCF7 cells showed an increased cell motility and invasion compared with vector control-expressing MCF7 cells in vitro.
source: Boyden chamber assay revealed that HTR2C expressing MCF7 cells showed an increased cell motility and invasion compared with vector control-expressing MCF7 cells in vitro (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a finding from the Boyden chamber assay shown in Figure 4D.

claim: In fish inoculated with HTR2C expressing MCF7 cells, the frequencies of fish showing head dissemination significantly increased to 96.7% ± 4.7% compared with 33.1% ± 18.5% in fish inoculated with vector control expressing MCF7 cells.
